knowledge_point.title: Finding Particular Solutions of Differential Equations by First Rearranging and Then Separating

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation ${e}^{(x - 2)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4(x - 2){e}^{(x - 2)}=1$ that satisfies $y(2)=7.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{(x - 2)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4(x - 2){e}^{(x - 2)} & =1 \\ {e}^{(x - 2)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1-4(x - 2){e}^{(x - 2)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{-(x - 2)}-4(x - 2) \\ \int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int ({e}^{-(x - 2)}-4(x - 2))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \,\text{d}y & =\int {e}^{-(x - 2)}\,\text{d}x-4\int (x - 2)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =-{e}^{-(x - 2)}-2{(x - 2)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(2)=7$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(2) & =7 \\ -{e}^{-0}-2\cdot {0}^{2}+C & =7 \\ C-1 & =7 \\ C & =8\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of ${e}^{(x - 2)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4(x - 2){e}^{(x - 2)}=1$ that satisfies the condition $y(2)=7$ is

$$
y=-{e}^{-(x - 2)}-2{(x - 2)}^{2}+8.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x - 2)}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8{(x - 2)}^{3} & =5 \\ {(x - 2)}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =5+8{(x - 2)}^{3} \\ \text{d}y & =(5{(x - 2)}^{-2}+8(x - 2))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \text{d}y & =\int (5{(x - 2)}^{-2}+8(x - 2))\,\text{d}x \\ y & =-5{(x - 2)}^{-1}+4{(x - 2)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(3)=6$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(3) & =6 \\ -5(1)^{-1}+4(1)^{2}+C & =6 \\ C-1 & =6 \\ C & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =-5{(x - 2)}^{-1}+4{(x - 2)}^{2}+7 \\  & =-\frac{5}{(x - 2)}+4{(x - 2)}^{2}+7.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(x + 4)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-4(x + 4)\sqrt{(x + 4)} & =3 \\ \sqrt{(x + 4)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3+4(x + 4)\sqrt{(x + 4)} \\ \text{d}y & =(3{(x + 4)}^{-1/2}+4(x + 4))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \text{d}y & =\int (3{(x + 4)}^{-1/2}+4(x + 4))\,\text{d}x \\ y & =6{(x + 4)}^{1/2}+2{(x + 4)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(-3)=11$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-3) & =11 \\ 6(1)^{1/2}+2(1)^{2}+C & =11 \\ C+8 & =11 \\ C & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =6{(x + 4)}^{1/2}+2{(x + 4)}^{2}+3 \\  & =6\sqrt{(x + 4)}+2{(x + 4)}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x - 3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)$ that satisfies $y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 3)={\pi }^{2}.$ Assume that $0<(x - 3)<\pi .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x - 3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)+8(x - 3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)}+8(x - 3) \\ \int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)}+8(x - 3))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \,\text{d}y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)}\,\text{d}x+8\int (x - 3)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)}\,\text{d}x+4{(x - 3)}^{2}+{C}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the integral on the right-hand side of this equality, we use a substitution

$$
u=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Then  we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+{C}_{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3))+{C}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where we used that $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)>0.$

Hence,

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3))+4{(x - 3)}^{2}+C.
$$

where $C={C}_{1}+{C}_{2}$ is an arbitrary constant. 

We now apply the initial condition $y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 3)={\pi }^{2}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 3) & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})+4{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡1+{\pi }^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x - 3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 3)$ that satisfies the condition $y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 3)={\pi }^{2}$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 3))+4{(x - 3)}^{2}.
$$
